people.bio:
AI Domestic Robotics Researcher, PhD candidate in Digital Humanities, University of Vienna, United States of America
Emily Kate Genatowski is an American immersive robotics researcher, historian, and entrepreneur based in Vienna, Austria, who has gained global recognition for her pioneering work in human-AI integration. Her unique research methodology explores the practical, legal, and social friction points that occur when developing technology moves out of laboratory environments and into everyday settings.
Genatowski achieved international prominence through a first-of-its-kind experiment, living full-time in her Vienna residence with "Tova," a Unitree bipedal humanoid robot. By treating her personal home as a robotics lab, she has documented the humanistic realities of sharing physical spaces with humanoid robotics; insights she shares on global stages, including her viral TED talk at TEDAI Vienna. This ongoing immersive ethnographic experiment has transformed her everyday life into inspiration for public discourse on the deployment of domestic humanoids. Emily speaks candidly on the psychological, behavioral, and practical realities of cohabitating with machines.
Before transitioning into immersive robotics research, Genatowski established a diverse career bridging digital humanities and corporate innovation. She holds an undergraduate degree in History from Columbia University and a Master’s degree from Harvard University. She formerly served as the North American coordinator for Google Arts & Culture, where she managed major digital collaborations with world-class institutions, including NASA, the Smithsonian, and the U.S. National Archives.
Currently a PhD candidate in Digital Humanities at the University of Vienna, she designed and taught the university's first academic master's course on AI and Large Language Models in Humanities Research and regularly consults with numerous other Viennese institutions on AI adoption policies. Emily speaks on stages and lecture halls across Europe about the many pain points of human robotic cohabitation and with a mind towards solution oriented thinking, has embarked upon both advocacy and entrepreneurial ventures. In addition to advocating for identity standards for autonomous robotics within the EU, Genatowski is also the founder of PSL, an Austria-based insurtech startup. PSL standardizes hundreds of risk variables across humanoid robotic deployments in five sectors. The confidence-weighted, multivariable risk scores enable specialist underwriters to develop insurance policies for autonomous robotics, helping modern society safely navigate the complex, evolving landscape of physical AI adoption.
people.name: Ms. Emily Kate Genatowski

people.bio:
Cristian León is the Founder and CEO of Drovid Technologies, a Chilean deep-tech company that uses autonomous drones and on-board artificial intelligence to protect forests by detecting risky human activity, the root cause of most wildfires, from the pre-ignition phase.
An electrical engineer by training, Cristian has more than a decade of experience in engineering, technology and entrepreneurship. In 2015 he founded an electrical engineering services company, and he has completed professional programs in technology development management (MIT) and intellectual property (Hong Kong University of Science and Technology).
In 2020 he founded Drovid with a simple question: what if we could stop a fire before it starts? Drovid’s AI operates directly on the drone, detecting risky human activity, smoke and fire, day and night. One of its models, AirWERD, was developed in collaboration with INRIA, which transferred 100% of the rights to Drovid. The technology has been validated in the field with the support of Chile’s national forestry corporation (CONAF) and investigative police (PDI), and has gained commercial validation through a pilot on 2,500 hectares with Forestal Santa Blanca. A second phase is now starting to validate operations, including a latest-generation model that contextualizes human risk, under the Startup Ciencia 2026 grant. A PCT patent application is in progress in dozens of countries.
Cristian represented Chile at the COP28 business mission and, in 2025 and 2026, was nominated by Chile’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs as the country’s representative for the APEC Bio-Circular-Green Award. He is a member of the Sustainable Forest Future Roundtable (Proyecta Chile 2050), where he promotes a prevention-first approach to wildfires. In 2026, Drovid was the winner of the WIPO Global Awards in the ICT startup category.
He leads Drovid’s intellectual property strategy and sustainability vision, with the conviction that protecting nature is not a cost but one of the greatest opportunities of our generation.
people.name: Mr. Cristian Léon

people.bio:
Executive Director, Public Affairs and Media Policy, WAN-IFRA, World Association of News Publishers, France.
Elena Perotti is Executive Director of Media Policy and Public Affairs at WAN-IFRA, the World Association of News Publishers, representing more than 20,000 media brands and 60 national publishers' associations in 120 countries.. For 20 years at WAN-IFRA she has been the person in charge of the relationship with the global community of WAN-IFRA member associations of news media publishers, and main liaison with the organisation's governing bodies. For over a decade she has studied and advocated on the relationship between big tech and publishers on behalf of WAN-IFRA's members, developing an early specialisation in how AI is reshaping the news publishing business. She leads WAN-IFRA's regular policy briefings, keeping members promptly informed of the most relevant global media policy developments and giving them exclusive access to experts, and holds executive briefings for publisher CEOs on the role of policy in shaping the (emerging AI) content marketplace. She represents the industry before international bodies including the UN, WIPO, UNESCO, IGF, and the Council of Europe, and serves on the Advisory Group of the M20, a global initiative driving information integrity, AI governance, and press freedom within the G20 framework https://media20.org/about/#m20advisorygroup. A frequent speaker at conferences worldwide, she also oversees WAN-IFRA's News Literacy initiatives. She holds a Master's degree in International Trade Law.

people.bio:
Anderson Rocha is Full-Professor of Artificial Intelligence and Digital Forensics at the Institute of Computing, University of Campinas (Unicamp), Brazil. He is an IEEE Fellow and an IEEE Biometrics Council Distinguished Lecturer. He is the Head of the Artificial Intelligence Lab., Recod.ai, at Unicamp. He is an elected affiliate of the Brazilian Academy of Sciences

(ABC) and the Brazilian Academy of Forensic Sciences (ABC). He is a threeterm elected member of the IEEE Information Forensics and Security Technical Committee (IFSTC) and a two-term chair of such committee. He has actively been an editor of important international journals and the chair of key conferences in Al and digital forensics. He is a Microsoft Research and a Google Research Faculty Fellow, important academic recognitions given to researchers by Microsoft Research and Google. In addition, in 2016, he was awarded the Tan Chin Tuan (TCT) Fellowship, a recognition promoted by the Tan Chin Tuan Foundation in Singapore. Since 2023, he is also an Asia Pacific Artificial Intelligence Association Fellow. He has been the principal investigator of several research projects in partnership with public funding agencies in Brazil and abroad and national and multi-national companies, having already filed and licensed several patents. He is ranked among the Top 2% of research scientists worldwide according to PlosOne/Stanford and Research.com studies. Finally, he is now a LinkedIn Top Voice in Artificial Intelligence for continuously raising awareness of Al and its potential impacts on society at large scale.
people.name: Mr Anderson Rocha

people.bio:
Andres GUADAMUZ GONZALEZ


Reader in Intellectual Property Law at the University of Sussex and Editor in Chief of the Journal of World Intellectual Property, Costa Rica


Andres is a Reader in Intellectual Property Law at the University of Sussex and the Editor in Chief of the Journal of World Intellectual Property. His main research areas are on artificial intelligence and copyright, open licensing, and smart contracts. He has written two books and over 40 articles and book chapters, and also blogs regularly about different technology regulation topics.
people.name: Mr. Andres Guadamuz

people.bio:
Professor of Law, East China University of Political 
Science and Law, Shanghai, China
Wang Qian is a professor of law and the Vice Chairman of the 
Academic Committee in East China University of Political 
Science and Law.  He also serves as the Vice Chairman of the 
China Copyright Association.  He received his LL.M from the 
University of Toronto in Canada and his Ph.D. from Peking 
University.  He published the book Study on Exclusive Rights of 
Copyright in the Network Environment, Protection and 
Regulation of Technological Measures in the Copyright Law, 
and Copyright Protection on the Internet.  His textbook 
Intellectual Property Law Course (1-8 editions) is one of the  
most popular IP textbooks in China.  Mr. Wang acts as a consulting expert for many courts and procuratorates, including the Beijing Higher People’s Court, Shanghai People’s Procuratorate and Shanghai Intellectual Property Court. 
He participated in the drafting of the Regulations on the Protection of Information Network Transmission Rights and is a member of the Expert Committee for the third revision of the Copyright Law.  He was honored as one of the Top Ten Outstanding Young Jurists in the Ninth National Awards.
people.name: Mr. Wang Qian

people.bio: Dr. Rachel Free is a partner in the patent team at International Law Firm CMS where she helps clients to protect their technology through patents. She has an MSc in Artificial Intelligence and a DPhil in Vision Science. She qualified as a European and UK patent attorney in the last century and has worked on AI patent drafting and prosecution through her career. Rachel is a member of the All Party Parliamentary Group on AI (APPG AI) which advises parliamentarians regarding AI. She is vice Chair of the Chartered Institute of Patent Attorneys (CIPA) computer technology committee.
people.name: Ms. Rachel Free

people.bio:
Director, IP and Frontier
Technologies Division, Infrastructure and Platforms Sector,
WIPO, Geneva

Dr. Ulrike Till is the Director of the IP and Frontier Technologies Division at WIPO.

She is anexperienced IP and patent lawyer with significant commercial background and exposure to complex
international patent litigation, data exclusivity issues, commercial negotiations, competition law, settlements and agreements. In her current role, Ulrike focus on the wide reaching IP policy implications arising from digitalization, industry 4.0 and frontier technologies.

Ulrike is qualified both as an English solicitor and German Rechtsanwalt and has practiced in both jurisdictions. She has a technical background with a PhD in Chemistry, management training
people.name: Ms. Ulrike Till
